subject: Thanksgiving 2026 storms
title: Thanksgiving storm forecast: Where will it hit? Both coasts, Wed–Fri
answer: Two storm systems threaten Thanksgiving travel in 2026. An atmospheric river is soaking Northern California, Oregon and Washington on Tuesday and Wednesday, Nov. 24–25, while a coastal storm brings heavy rain to the Southeast on Wednesday and wind and rain to the Northeast on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26.
in_the_news: AAA expects 81.5 million Americans to travel at least 50 miles between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30, and the worst weather lines up with the busiest days. Forecasters say the East Coast storm's track can still shift.
body:
On the West Coast, a strong Pacific storm fed by an atmospheric river is bringing heavy rain, gusty winds and mountain snow from Northern California to Washington, Yahoo News reported. The greatest impacts are expected Tuesday and Wednesday along Interstate 5 and on mountain routes such as I-80 over the Sierra Nevada, where heavy snow can bring chain controls or closures. Flooding and mudslides are possible. Southern California should miss the heaviest rain.

In the East, a storm is forecast to take shape near Florida on Wednesday, ABC News reported, with 2 to 4 inches of rain possible in South Florida and rain spreading from Florida to Virginia and west toward Illinois and Indiana. Coastal gusts in the Carolinas could top 50 mph. On Thursday, a high wind watch covers New York City and Philadelphia for the whole holiday, with gusts up to 60 mph possible, plus moderate to major coastal flooding from Virginia to New York around morning high tide. The National Weather Service in Boston warned of a potentially significant coastal storm from Thanksgiving into Friday, with some snow or ice possible in the interior Northeast and the Appalachians.

What it means for your trip: Tuesday — allow extra time on I-5 and I-80 in Northern California and the Pacific Northwest; Seattle and San Francisco flights may be delayed. Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year — thunderstorms could slow the Atlanta and Charlotte hubs, and delays there tend to spread nationwide. Thursday — expect wind and heavy rain on I-95 from Washington to Boston; coastal roads such as those in Atlantic City may flood near high tide. Friday — rain lingers from the Great Lakes to Maine while Philadelphia and New York dry out. Most of the 81.5 million travelers, 72.9 million by AAA's count, will drive; about 5.96 million will fly. Airlines often issue travel waivers before major storms that let passengers change flights without a fee, so check your airline's app before leaving for the airport.

What comes next: forecasters say another storm could form in the East during the return weekend of Nov. 28–29, and more Pacific storms could reach the West Coast. The forecast for the Thanksgiving Day storm is likely to sharpen by Wednesday.

faq.q: Will the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons fly?
faq.a: It depends on the wind. New York City rules ground the giant balloons if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph. A high wind watch is in effect for Thursday, so a decision may come the morning of the 100th parade.

faq.q: Which airports could see the most delays?
faq.a: Seattle and San Francisco on Tuesday, Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday, and the New York, Philadelphia and Boston airports on Thursday.

faq.q: How many people are traveling for Thanksgiving 2026?
faq.a: AAA projects 81.5 million, about 0.1% fewer than last year's record of 81.6 million.

faq.q: Is the East Coast storm a tropical storm?
faq.a: No. The National Hurricane Center said on Nov. 22 that the system was unlikely to become tropical or subtropical, but it can still bring strong gusts, rough surf and heavy rain.
